title: Large Language Models for Title and Abstract Screening in Systematic Reviews: A Systematic Review
objective: To evaluate the accuracy of large language models (LLMs) in performing title and abstract screening for systematic reviews.
population: Large language models (LLMs) used for screening titles and abstracts in systematic reviews.
intervention_or_concept: Application of LLMs for title and abstract screening in systematic reviews.
comparator: Traditional screening methods (e.g., manual screening by reviewers, rule-based screening tools).
outcomes: Sensitivity of LLMs in identifying relevant studies.
Specificity of LLMs in excluding irrelevant studies.
Overall accuracy of LLMs in title and abstract screening.
Inter-rater agreement between LLMs and human reviewers.
Time efficiency of LLMs compared to traditional methods.
context: Systematic reviews in health and social sciences where LLMs are used for title and abstract screening.

inclusion.text: Studies that evaluate the performance of large language models (LLMs) in title and abstract screening for systematic reviews.
Studies that report sensitivity, specificity, or overall accuracy metrics for LLMs in screening tasks.
Studies that compare LLMs with traditional screening methods (e.g., manual screening, rule-based tools).
Studies published in peer-reviewed journals, conference proceedings, or grey literature in English.

exclusion.text: Studies that do not use LLMs for title and abstract screening (e.g., studies using only rule-based or manual screening).
Studies that focus on full-text screening or data extraction rather than title and abstract screening.
Studies that do not report performance metrics (e.g., sensitivity, specificity, accuracy) for LLMs.
Studies that are not available in English.
Studies that are not peer-reviewed or are not published in the specified timeframe (2020 onwards).

study_designs: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LLMs with traditional methods.
Observational studies reporting LLM performance metrics.
Simulation studies or computational models evaluating LLM accuracy.
rob_domains: Dataset representativeness: Whether the training and test datasets are representative of the target population of systematic reviews.
Reference standard: Whether a gold standard (e.g., expert review) is used to assess LLM performance.
Leakage: Whether there is any data leakage between training and testing phases.
Reporting of metrics: Whether the study reports sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and inter-rater agreement.
Reproducibility: Whether the study provides sufficient detail to reproduce the LLM screening process.
synthesis_plan: A meta-analysis will be conducted to pool sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy metrics across studies. Subgroup analyses will be performed based on study design, LLM type, and screening context. Risk-of-bias assessments will be conducted using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool for RCTs and a modified version for other study designs. Narrative synthesis will be used to summarize findings on the accuracy and utility of LLMs in title and abstract screening for systematic reviews.
